name: surprises-2
statement: The functional part of the RL-Zero-Math weight change is a high-rank, strongly nonlinear change (spread over thousands of singular directions per matrix, concentrated in a small set of neurons that act through the model's outlier channels, and altering the computation of each solution step rather than writing a deliberation/answer-format readout), while the low-rank head that stands out above the null is incidental optimizer drift that does almost nothing; so neuron subsets ranked by weight change fail (the carrying neurons are not the most-changed ones and act only jointly, not additively), DARE works (it keeps the full-rank remainder's per-matrix structure and its magnitude, which is what carries the effect, while scrambling the low-rank head), accuracy rises in proportion to the dose with no plateau, and RL does reorganise neuron features on general text.
scope: Olmo-3-1025-7B base vs Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math (step 2,800), all 2-D weight matrices; MATH-500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 (n13 setting) and T 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3. Does not cover SFT deltas, the 1B Bolmo grafts, other model families, or the cue and sampling results.

explains.quote: 11.8% of its squared norm sits in 8 singular directions per matrix
explains.how: 88% of the delta's energy lies outside the top 8 directions; the head is a predictable artefact of Adam's per-coordinate scaling, and the function sits in the full-rank bulk where almost all the change is.

explains.quote: Late-MLP top directions x base lm_head read as deliberation words
explains.how: The head reads as deliberation words in Math-RL and Code-RL alike, so it is a generic RL style drift shared across tasks, not the math skill, which lives in the task-specific high-rank bulk.
Ranking by weight change picks the wrong neurons: the carrying set is small but is not the most-changed set, so top-changed and random neurons both miss it.
DARE keeps each matrix's full-rank structure and multiplies its magnitude, so the high-rank part that carries the function survives while the low-rank head is scrambled.

explains.quote: yet it scores like the whole MLP delta
explains.how: Function depends on the full-rank pattern spread over every entry of every matrix; DARE's sample reproduces that pattern in each matrix, so 33-1,000x the energy scores like the whole delta while a low-rank projection of the same delta would not.

explains.quote: Every arm that recovers accuracy also takes RL's format and length
explains.how: Format and length come along with any large full-rank change. They are a separate side effect of the same perturbation and do not cause the accuracy gain.

explains.quote: the RL change is NOT concentrated in MLP neurons
explains.how: Weight-change energy is flat by construction of the optimizer, so it says nothing about where function is; the carrying neurons are few and invisible to an energy ranking.

explains.quote: 88 % of all 352,256 neurons have a positive score
explains.how: First-order scores are positive almost everywhere because a teacher-forced gradient spreads credit, but the 0.708-nat gap is a quarter unexplained by the sum, the signature of joint, nonlinear action.
Only the first-order part adds up; the remaining 0.16 nats appear only when neurons and attention change together, as in the 1B graft's interaction term.

explains.quote: RL barely moves which tokens a neuron fires on most
explains.how: 2.11 changed slots is 2.5x the noise floor in every band and rises with depth: RL measurably re-sorts neuron features even on general text.

explains.quote: diverge on math solutions, more with depth
explains.how: The divergence is as large on the base's own text as on RL's, so it is a change in how every step is computed, compounding with depth, not a readout engaged by deliberation contexts.
Coordinated sub-ulp moves over billions of entries add up to a large full-rank change in each layer's output: the bulk is small per entry but large in aggregate.

explains.quote: Mean KL per token after the cue 0.06-0.09 nats
explains.how: Small per-token KL spread over positions that depend on context is what a high-rank, input-dependent change produces; a fixed low-rank readout would put the KL at a few format tokens.

conflicts.how: DARE copies of a fine-tune delta destroy the 1B Bolmo model; the theory needs the SFT delta's threshold to sit far above its energy, which is not measured.
The theory predicts accuracy rising in proportion to dose up to 1 and beyond; a peak below 1 (on an SFT delta) does not fit.

conflicts.quote: Edit minus norm-matched random: +1.7 points [-1.7, +5.0], not separated
conflicts.how: Consistent with magnitude mattering, but the theory also needs the direction of the full-rank bulk to matter, and here direction added nothing measurable.
The published view fits full-rank function, but uniform spread over layers sits uneasily with the claim that a small neuron set carries the effect.
Energy is spread over many components as the theory says, but energy spread alone does not show that function follows it.

rival: Low-rank linear function: a few coherent singular directions per matrix carry the gain and the high-rank remainder is noise. It predicts that a rank-8 truncation of each matrix's delta recovers most of the gain (near RL, with RL's format) and that the high-rank remainder recovers almost none; this theory predicts the opposite.

predictions.experiment: Base + rank-8 SVD truncation of (RL - base) in every 2-D matrix, plain prompt, MATH-500 n=500, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, cap 16,384, grader v3, one sample (endpoints v3: base 305, RL 464)
predictions.refuted_by: more than 360 right, or 'Answer:' line in fewer than 20 % of answers (RL-like format)

predictions.experiment: Base + (delta minus its rank-8 truncation) in every 2-D matrix, same setting
predictions.refuted_by: fewer than 400 right: the high-rank remainder would then not carry the gain

predictions.experiment: Base + random rank-8 update per matrix with the same per-matrix Frobenius norm as the rank-8 truncation, same setting
predictions.refuted_by: a gap of more than 30 right to the true rank-8 truncation in either direction: the head would then not be incidental

predictions.experiment: Base + rank-1 SVD truncation of (RL - base) in every 2-D matrix, same setting
Base + 0.5 * (RL - base), plain prompt, MATH-500 n=500, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, cap 16,384, grader v3
predictions.refuted_by: more than 420 right (a wide plateau along the direction)
